title: Choosing the Right Azure Service
description: Compare common Azure services and match them to ASP.NET Core application requirements.

data.text: Azure has hundreds of services, but ASP.NET Core developers typically use a small set. Choosing the right service affects cost, scale, and how much code you have to write.

rows: Host a web API or MVC app

data.text: Imagine a simple blog API. Each concern maps cleanly to one Azure service.

items: **App Service** hosts the ASP.NET Core API
**Azure SQL Database** stores posts and comments
**Key Vault** stores the database connection string

items.question: Should I use App Service or Azure Functions?
items.answer: Use App Service when you have a long-running web app or API. Use Functions for event-driven, short-lived background work.

items.question: When should I choose Cosmos DB over Azure SQL?
items.answer: Choose Cosmos DB for globally distributed, schema-flexible data. Choose Azure SQL for relational data with strong consistency and mature tooling.

data.title: Quick Reference
points: App Service = web apps and APIs
Blob Storage = files and binary data
data.takeaway: Start small. Most ASP.NET Core apps begin with App Service, Azure SQL, and Blob Storage, then add caching, queues, and monitoring as needed.
